messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: numerically ordered data
parts:
On Tue, Mar 15, 2016 at 10:09 AM, Third Jacob <fourt...@gmail.com> wrote:
:-)

function: mirt
arguments: data: "a matrix or data.frame that consists of numerically ordered data"

I was wondering whether this was related to the fact that the order of EAPs which are returned by fscores don't follow the same order as my original data?
Anyway, what would the easiest way to sort the fscores-EAPs back to the order of my original data?

It has more to do with R object types, where correct incorrect is stored as 0/1, for example (if you scored it 1/0 then the slopes would just switch signs). It's stated this way because a data input consisting of c('correct', 'incorrect') or ordered(c('low', 'med', 'high')) is not supported. Mostly because I'm lazy, but also because standard operations likes sums makes little sense with factors/ordered variables.

Phil

Thanks

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: numerically ordered data
parts:
I'm not sure what you mean, the EAPs are in the original order.

dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod <- mirt(dat, 1)
full <- cbind(dat, fscores(mod, method = 'EAP'))
head(full)

Phil

mod9eap <- fscores(mod9)

>  which(apply(mod9eap$D1[,1:200],1,function(gg) identical(as.numeric(gg),as.numeric(resp1[1,1:200]))))

...
and so on...
rows are completely shuffled after fscores...?!

messages.subject: Re: numerically ordered data

What version of mirt are you using? That seems like very old behaviour (what you're seeing is a collapsed table of responses, not the individual patterns). You may need to pass full.scores = TRUE to fix this, or just update.

Phil
